page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a local 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench scores generally fall within the average range. Memory performance is a notable strength, with PassMark memory scores and large-block write bandwidth ranking in the top 25%, though read-only bandwidth remains average. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks perform strongly, but multi-threaded decompression and database operations show weaker relative performance, landing in the bottom 25%. LLM inference speeds are average for small models but drop to the bottom 10% for prompt processing on medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and bundled NVMe storage, making it a resource-dense option for memory-heavy workloads without the premium of a fully dedicated high-core count bare-metal system. However, the tradeoff lies in its moderate multi-core processing power and lower database operation throughput. This configuration is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, software compilation, and general-purpose workloads that benefit from high single-core performance and fast local storage, rather than highly parallelized database transactions or large-scale LLM inference.
